text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Christopher de Souza –  38 To ask the Minister for Home Affairs what are the reasons for not publicly disclosing the figures on the racial composition of the prison inmate population and criminal offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In all these matters of public disclosure, for that matter, any other Government action, any decision by the Government has to be guided by what is in the public interest and that includes assessing what information should be made public.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And, really, we do not take an ideological position on these matters.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, in certain respects, releasing data can adversely impact the community and society and this particular question relates to one such example.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I say "deepen", specifically because it is not as if these stereotypes do not exist.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our concern is releasing the data would deepen those stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, if Government were to release data on racial composition of our prison inmate population and criminal offenders on a regular basis, we really risk hardening the stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Over time, the concern is that that will undermine our efforts in building harmonious relations amongst all the races and, really, will make it harder for us to achieve racial harmony.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is not to say that the Government does not release any race-based statistics at all.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have done so in our population census, which includes key indicators broken down by ethnicity, like resident population, marriage and fertility, education, home ownership and religion.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Through the M3 network, the initiative by Minister Masagos, we have also released specific statistics on the Malay community, like the number of Malay graduates from Institutes of Higher Learning, the number of Malay professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) and the recidivism rate of the Malay inmate population.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government also releases race-based statistics on drug and inhalant abuse through CNB’s annual reports.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Why do we, for example, release those statistics?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We do so to effectively mobilise the communities into action.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: By working with the community, we are then able to come up with interventions that are better suited for different communities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: While I deal with this, I should also say that the Malay and Indian communities have seen improvements in terms of educational attainment and literacy rates over the last decade.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Malay community has made significant progress: the number of Malay university graduates has doubled and the proportion of Malays working as PMETs has also increased.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Going back to the point on releasing data on drug and inhalant abuse and whether this could lead to stereotyping, the answer is yes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our assessment is that in these cases, the upside of spurring the community to take action outweighs the negative of potentially deepening the stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We consider the implications on each community and proceed based on judgement and assessment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Dadah Itu Haram campaign and the Malay-Muslim Organisations (MMO) Rehabilitation Network are examples of how the Government was able to partner the Malay community to join hands with CNB and Singapore Prison Service (SPS) to combat drug abuse and prevent reoffending.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen positive results with our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In some other instances, the judgment lies in not releasing the data.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Annex 1 sets out the list of stakeholders we engaged with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We specifically went and asked the various community organisations on their views on releasing such information: race-based statistics on criminal offenders and inmate population.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We consulted many different groups and community leaders, sought their views.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And it would encourage stereotypes and harm community relations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of their comments I have asked to be reproduced for Members’ reference.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members can cast their eyes over the slide.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It may be too simplistic to share these race-based statistics as the reality is more complex.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another commented, "It is not good to publicise such statistics, no matter which community is involved." Members can see the different comments.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They said you should not simply look at the racial breakdown.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It would not take into account other contributing factors which could have led to a person committing a crime.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It would also detract from the improvements made by the respective communities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Overall, they agreed that the race-based inmate and crime statistics should continue to be shared in closed-door settings with community leaders and groups, so that we can address the issues as a community.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is the Government's as well as the community leaders’ considered assessment that race-based inmate and offender statistics should not be released.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will continue our current approach of disclosing such information on a selective basis, where doing so would be useful and positive for the community and society.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If any Member has a different view, having heard the views of the community leaders, you are welcome to explain why.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I completely agree with the stance of MHA.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Minister share with the House how do specific communities work behind the scenes, perhaps in the prisons, to address some of these issues?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For Prisons, the tagline is "Captains of Lives" because we no longer look at prison as a place where we just guard people.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And those with family support, those who have other kinds of community support including religious support, we find that the recidivism rates are generally lower.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, what is necessary also beyond prisons officers, MHA officers and civil servants doing it is a substantial community support when they are in prison and when they are out of prison.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, in prison, for example, if you take the different communities, on a non-religious based approach, we have a wide variety of volunteers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But, of course, many religious groups also come in and offer their services and we find that they actually make a big difference.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They go in there, there is intervention with religious education, there is intervention with social skills.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The churches play an extremely active role in helping inmates, both when they are in and when they are out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we have a lot of people who are, what I would call, true activists.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They want to make a difference to people's lives.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix, unless Members had asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn.]
